name: Erenumab
owner: Amgen (US); Novartis (outside the US and Japan)

discovery.note: A fully human IgG2 antibody developed in transgenic mice against the canonical CGRP receptor; co-developed with Novartis.

tagline: First CGRP-pathway antibody for migraine prevention
summary: Erenumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that blocks the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor. Approved in 2018, it was the first medicine designed specifically to prevent migraine.
mechanism: CGRP released from trigeminal nerve endings drives meningeal vasodilation and pain signalling during migraine. Erenumab binds the CGRP receptor complex (calcitonin receptor-like receptor with RAMP1), preventing CGRP from activating it.

It is the only approved CGRP antibody that targets the receptor; fremanezumab, galcanezumab and eptinezumab bind the CGRP ligand. Blocking CGRP's vasodilator role may explain reports of constipation and hypertension.
uses: Preventive treatment of migraine in adults

history.title: STRIVE
history.detail: Phase 3 results (Goadsby et al., NEJM) show reduced monthly migraine days versus placebo.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: In May Aimovig becomes the first FDA-approved anti-CGRP therapy; EU approval follows in July.

history.title: Label update and partner dispute
history.detail: Constipation with serious complications is added to the label; Amgen and Novartis begin litigation over their collaboration.

history.title: Hypertension warning
history.detail: The FDA adds hypertension to the warnings section.

history.title: HER-MES
history.detail: A head-to-head trial finds erenumab better tolerated and more effective than topiramate for migraine prevention.

facts: The CGRP pathway in migraine was proposed in the 1980s–90s by Lars Edvinsson and Peter Goadsby; they were among four migraine researchers awarded the 2021 Brain Prize.
